articleTitle: Frequency Symbolic Analysis of Linear Periodically Time-Variable Circuits by Sub-Circuits Method
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: frequency symbolic method (FS method) of the analysis of the steady-state mode of linear periodically time-variable (LPTV) circuits is intended to form their transmission functions in frequency domain. The transmission functions are approximated by Fourier polynomials and contain a complex variable, time variable and parameters of circuit elements in the form of symbols. The coefficients of such Fourier polynomials by the FS-method are unknown in the symbolic systems of linear algebraic equations (SSLAE), and are defined as their solutions in symbolic form. An obvious disadvantage of solving SSLAE is a significant increase in the required computer time with an increase in the number of unknowns. In research paper, the reduction of SSLAE solution time has been achieved by using one of the sub-circuit methods, namely, the d-trees method. The d-trees method was developed for circuits with constant parameters, so the paper considers its extension, the so-called matrix method of d-trees, to the circuits with variable parameters. The matrix method of d-trees provides close to optimal rendering of similar ones in formed algebraic expressions, which leads to a significant reduction in their formation time. The analysis of the given examples of chain circuits with variable parameters has shown a significant gain in time (hundreds and thousands of times) using the matrix method of d-trees than with standard MATLAB tools. This reduction of time allows to expand significantly the scope of application of the FS method in the problems of statistical research or optimization of electronic devices that are modelled by linear parametric circuits.

Author Keywords: linear circuits linear periodically time-variable circuits

articleTitle: Personal fall detector using MEMS sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents a human fall detection system. The system uses measurement data from accelerometer and gyroscope mounted on a hip belt of a monitored person. The data is wirelessly transmitted via WiFi and M QTT protocol to the server where it is analyzed and possibly the selected caregiver is notified about the fall. This message reaches the caregiver via the mobile application. After the test, the efficiency of the whole system can be estimated at 88%, but the efficiency of not detecting a fall (not raising false positive alarms) was 100%.

articleTitle: Numerical adjustment of Ion Parametric Resonance conditions for biological experiments
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This article deals with the practical adjustment of the static magnetic field, which would possibly lead to clarification of special conditions used during experiments focused on Ion parametric resonance theory. While the targeted ion in the cell oscillates proportionally to the frequency of the applied time-varying magnetic field, even low alteration of Earth magnetic flux density could modify or slightly shift the resonance peak. Therefore, numerical simulations of the designed experimental setup, with a focus on 5 different evaluation curves of B-field, were performed. The extraction curves' positions represent the Yeast-Peptone-Dextrose medium, where eukaryotic cells are cultivated. After time exposure to the applied magnetic field with defined parameters, the proliferative activity is calculated. As a result of the unexpected diversity of previous studies in relevance to IPR theory, we have decided to modify and create unique conditions with an increasing static component of the magnetic field to 5.02 mT. Consequently, the alteration of Earth's magnetic field in time will be negligible to our conditions.

articleTitle: Non-invasive PD measurement method in air-insulated switchgear - signal processing
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article contains the results of partial discharges (PD) measurements of several types (high potential, low potential) of Medium Voltage (MV) air-insulated switchgear. For this purpose, Transient Earth Voltage (TEV) sensors and High Frequency Current Transformer (HFCT) were used. The obtained signal was processed by wavelet transform in Wavelet Signal Denoiser MATLAB build-in application. The result will be a further point in the research - collecting data from real PD measurement objects, proper classification using artificial intelligence and finally create cheap universal sensor for long-term online monitoring.

articleTitle: Exposure modelling to child's and adult's chest to EMF inside shielded areas
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The effects of electromagnetic (EM) fields on a model of a child's and adult's chest in the shielded areas of a cellar and the compartment of a railway wagon are discussed in this work. Electromagnetic modeling based on the Finite Integration approach was used in this study. The simulations were run for a specific scenario in which the individual models were positioned in various shaded areas as close to the EM radiation source as possible. A PIF A antenna operating at 900 and 1800 MHz provided the radio frequency source for the EM field. The results were examined in terms of SAR values by measuring the absorption of EM radiation inside the chests of a toddler and an adult. The SAR values for the child chest model were higher than for the adult chest model, according to the results.

articleTitle: Melanoma recognition using deep learning and ensemble of classifiers
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents the special arrangement of an ensemble of classifiers for melanoma recognition. It is based on the application of deep learning. The study applies the structure of the convolutional neural network to create the numerical descriptors of dermoscopic images of melanoma. The flattened vector of image descriptors is subjected to diagnostic feature selection by applying different selection methods. As a result, different sets of a limited number of diagnostic features are generated. In the next stage, these sets of features represent the input attributes for two types of classical classifiers: support vector machine and random forest of decision trees. An additional set of softmax classifiers supplied by a set of features randomly selected from the available descriptors is also applied. By combining different selection methods with these classifiers an ensemble classification system is created and integrated by majority voting. Thanks to the fusion of results of many classifiers forming an ensemble the accuracy and all other quality measures have been significantly increased in the recognition of melanoma from non-melanoma images.

Index Terms: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve

articleTitle: The principle of prediction of complex time-dependent nonlinear problems using RNN
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: An approach based on recurrent neural networks (RNN s) is applied to verify the possibility of using surrogate models for the prediction of dynamic nonlinear problems. Modeling complex time dependencies is currently still a challenge, when the structure of the neural network needs to be adapted to the dynamics of the problem. In this paper, the possibility of using prediction in space-time problems is illustrated by the possibility of using it to predict the course of the current in a simple RL circuit that is powered by a voltage source.

articleTitle: Improvement of Insulator Image Processing Using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Insulator fault within the transmission lines is the main consideration in power transmission accidents. The photographs captured from the aerial inspection will be utilized to detect the fault of insulators for further maintenance. To verify the effectiveness of insulator detection methods supported by deep learning, we tested and compared the great performance of 4 state-of-the-art deep-learning-based detectors with different characteristics. Damaged insulators seriously threaten the safe operation of power transmission lines. This paper proposes an insulation fault detection method supported by some deep learning state-of-art algorithms. This aim provides a reference for intelligent inspection and defect detection of insulators and vibration dampers on transmission lines.

articleTitle: Forecasting of Dynamic Processes in Electrical Engineering Using Discrete Macromodeling
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The growing need to increase the energy efficiency of power supply systems and the use of innovative technologies, require adequate and accurate determination of consumed and generated electricity. To solve the problem of forecasting, it is proposed to carry out mathematical macro modeling using discrete autonomous macromodels in the form of a “black box” with subsequent adaptation of the models to computer simulation tools. An example of the model of short-term energy consumption of an electric power facility using a discrete macromodel in the form of state variables is considered.

articleTitle: Numerical Model of Realistic Human Head Phantom
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article focuses on developing a simulation model of the realistic shape human head phantom used for investigating the influence of the electromagnetic field on the human body and the processes taking place in it. The introductory part is reserved to describing the modelled antennas and the human head phantom itself. The results of numerical simulations and measurements on a realistic human head phantom are compared.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks - Deterministic Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Chaotic states can occur in the convolutional neural network, which are caused by both an increase in the learning speed and an increase in the values of the filters in the convolutional layers. The appearance of local minima due to the increase in the speed of learning causes the appearance of bifurcations on the dependence of learning error on the number of epochs.

articleTitle: Using Surrogate Model for Shape Optimization of Busbar
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Methodology of shape optimization of the frequency converter blades, which are heated by Joule losses due to nonuniform current flow, is presented. For processing this coupled and nonlinear problem, its full mathematical model is replaced by a suitable equivalent model, on which the optimization is subsequently performed. The paper demonstrates the possibilities of acceleration of complete simulations, where it is often problematic to carry out the optimization process, using a suitable equivalent model, which would be able to provide sufficiently accurate results in the initial design stages.

articleTitle: Adaptive Model of Battery System Behavior for Electromobility
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to optimize comparative value predicting the remaining electric vehicle's range. The paper deals with the mathematical model for a typical battery system used in electro mobility, in accordance with the real operating parameters, actual battery state, track profile, and ambient conditions. Raspberry Pi Pico microcontroller board is used to obtain and process the necessary operational data.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the kidney
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This work describes proposed set of steps that need to be taken in order to create and visualise spatial models of the kidney from macroscopic histopathological examination data. We discuss the way of converting examination scans into compressed, computer processable files, method of determining border-points on each layer and creating intermediate layers between them. Finally, we want to present method of visualising processed scans into 3D representation of the kidney. Significant factor that impacts our results is very limited number of scans, that reduces precision of the final 3D reconstruction.

articleTitle: Conductometry as an evaluation tool in research into the impact of low-frequency electromagnetic field irradiation on cells
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The proposed paper proves the suitability of using a conductivity value of the solution as reference information in determining the change in the number of cells in the solution as a response to the acting low-frequency electromagnetic field irradiation. The experiment is performed using three types of liquid solutions in three types of environments. As a model organism is used yeasts Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The results show that measuring the conductivity of a yeast solution using a commercially available laboratory conductometer has certain limitations and is not suitable for determining the number of yeast cells in the solution.

articleTitle: Design and construction of a Railgun
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This article deals with the issue of designing and constructing a prototype of a Railgun working on low voltage supplied by a battery of supercapacitors. It describes problems accompanying such tasks and it presents results obtained during testing of the prototype.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of electric arc by simulation tests and practical measurements of a simple relay
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The electric arc is a very complex phenomenon, therefore numerical modeling is not an easy issue. The aim of this article is to present the phenomenon known as showering arc and to compare the results obtained during laboratory measurements with simulations using ready-made element offered in the program Matlab Simulink. This phenomenon is based on a rapid ignition and extinguishing of the electric arc between the relay contacts when opening them. The effect of this phenomenon are electromagnetic disturbances, the maximum voltage of which might be many times greater than the nominal voltage. For this reason, these disturbances may cause malfunctioning electronic devices or lead to its damage.

articleTitle: Interactive Visualization of Agent-Based Pandemic Simulation in Web Browser
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents a web-based system designed to visualize a simulation of ca. 500,000 residents of a city during the COVID-19 outbreak. Each agent's infection status and mobility are presented in the time scale. The main effort was to ensure simplicity from the user's perspective and smooth operation on various client devices. The full range of software engineering problems is discussed, from efficient data storage to optimization of visualization methods.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation of Artificial Notches Using Sweep Frequency Eddy Current Testing
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article deals with using the sweep frequency eddy current approach as an alternative method for material defect evaluation. The new eddy current probe is numerically modelled. Numerical investigations using CST Studio Suite are carried out to evaluate particular parameters of the selected approach. The obtained results are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Research on starting a group of induction motors of multi-motor electric drives
publicationTitle: 2022 23rd International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The sequence conditions for starting a group of induction motors are investigated. An algorithm and a computer program have been developed for numerical analysis of 1M's dynamic modes and static characteristics based on differential equations of electromechanical equilibrium written in d-q axes. On their basis, the dependences of electromagnetic torque of each motor on both slip and applied voltage, used for microprocessor control of the starting process and self-starting of a group of 1M, have been calculated.
